title: Customer activity update blocked by long-running PostgreSQL transaction
customer_impact: Updates targeting one hot customer-activity row are blocked while unrelated database queries and the wider ticket service remain available.
scope: Impact is isolated to transactions waiting on the same row-level lock. PostgreSQL is reachable and there is no evidence of database-wide saturation.

timeline.event: Customer-side update became blocked while the database health signal remained green.
L2 acknowledged the P3 degradation and captured transaction/lock evidence before remediation.
pg_stat_activity showed the waiting session in wait_event_type=Lock.
pg_blocking_pids() linked the waiting update to one named blocking transaction; pg_locks evidence was captured.
After targeted simulated approval, the confirmed blocker backend was terminated rather than restarting PostgreSQL.
The previously waiting UPDATE completed successfully and follow-up verification found no remaining lock waiter.

evidence: PostgreSQL remained reachable during the incident
waiter session identified by application_name opsforge-db002-waiter
pg_blocking_pids(waiter_pid) identified the named holder backend
pg_locks inventory captured for holder and waiter before remediation
only the confirmed blocking backend was terminated
waiting customer update completed with UPDATE 1 after blocker release
post-recovery blocked-session count returned to zero
post-recovery target-row update completed under a 2-second lock timeout
resolution: L2 proved a specific blocker-to-waiter lock relationship, captured lock evidence, and executed the approved simulated targeted blocker termination. The waiting transaction completed and a separate post-recovery update verified the row was writable without restarting PostgreSQL.
